mainTopic: Proving a כתובה claim with a גט, death witnesses, or several documents, and preventing a woman from collecting twice
overview: The amud opens by finishing the explanation of why a woman with a כתובה but no גט cannot collect: the husband can say he already paid her. The גמרא then rereads the whole משנה as the view of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. With no witnesses to the divorce she collects nothing. With witnesses she collects the תוספת, but the main sum only with a גט, and from the time of danger onward even without a גט. רב כהנא and רב אסי challenge רב's view that a גט collects the main sum: a widow might collect once with עדי מיתה and again with a hidden גט. The גמרא concludes that wherever there is no other protection, the court writes a שובר. מר קשישא then asks for the source that a widow from אירוסין gets a כתובה, and every proof is pushed off with 'maybe he wrote her one.' רב נחמן raises the worry that one גט could be used to collect in many courts. רב הונא answers that the court tears it and writes the reason on its back. Finally, a new משנה explains when a woman holding several גיטין and כתובות collects one or two כתובות, and the גמרא reconciles it with רב נחמן's rule that a second document cancels the first.

steps.title: The husband can claim he already paid
steps.stepSummary: The husband can say: I divorced her and gave her the money of her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He can say: I divorced her and gave her her כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its explanation of why the woman with a כתובה but no גט cannot collect. The husband has a believable claim that he already paid her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The woman holds the כתובה document but cannot show a גט. So the husband can claim that when he gave her the גט, he also paid the כתובה. The missing גט leaves room for his claim of payment.

keyTerms.meaning: He can say (he has a believable claim)
Marriage contract and the money it promises the wife

phrases.english: He can say:
phrases.notes: 'He' is the husband. The woman has the כתובה document but no גט.

phrases.english: I divorced her and gave her her marriage contract payment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the line of reasoning from before this section of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Without a גט, the husband can claim he already paid the כתובה when he divorced her.

steps.title: The end of the משנה shows there are witnesses to the divorce
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says that from the time of danger a woman collects without a גט. That only works if there are עדי גירושין, so the משנה must be dealing with such a case.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since the end of the משנה teaches, 'רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: From the time of danger and on, a woman collects her כתובה without a גט, and a lender collects without a פרוזבול,' we must be dealing with a case where there are witnesses to the divorce. For if there are no witnesses to the divorce, on what basis would she collect?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a difficulty. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's ruling at the end of the משנה only makes sense where there are witnesses to the divorce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without a גט and without witnesses, she has no proof she was ever divorced, so she could never collect. Since רבן שמעון בן גמליאל lets her collect without a גט, the משנה's case must have עדי גירושין. That clashes with the way the משנה was being read until now.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of a משנה
A document that keeps a loan from being canceled by שמיטה

steps.confusionAlert: Witnesses to the divorce prove she is divorced. They do not prove she was not already paid. That is why the גט itself still matters for the payment question.

phrases.english: But from the fact that the last clause teaches:
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
From the time of danger and onward,
phrases.notes: A time of persecution, when keeping legal documents was dangerous, so people did not hold on to them.

phrases.english: a woman collects her marriage contract without a bill of divorce,
and a creditor collects without a prosbol.
we are dealing with a case where there are witnesses to the divorce.
For if there are no witnesses to the divorce,
with what does she collect?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how the משנה was being read, based on its last clause.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of the משנה's case of a כתובה without a גט
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל lets her collect without a גט, which is only possible if there are עדי גירושין. So the משנה's case must include witnesses.

steps.title: The whole משנה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and is missing words
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the משנה. With no witnesses she collects nothing. With witnesses she collects the תוספת, and the main sum only if she shows a גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the whole משנה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, and it is missing words. This is what it teaches: These are not paid. When is this said? When there are no witnesses to the divorce. But if there are witnesses to the divorce, she collects the תוספת. And the main sum: if she shows a גט, she collects; if she does not show a גט, she does not collect.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the difficulty with a חסורי מיחסרא. It fills in missing words so the whole משנה becomes one view, that of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה now has levels. With no witnesses, she collects nothing. With witnesses, she collects the extra amount, the תוספת. For the main sum, the עיקר, she must still produce the גט. The witnesses prove the divorce, but only the גט protects the husband from being made to pay the main sum twice.

keyTerms.meaning: The text is missing words (and the גמרא fills them in)
The extra sum the husband added to the basic כתובה
The main, basic sum of the כתובה

steps.whyThisMatters: The גמרא often uses חסורי מיחסרא to solve a contradiction. It rebuilds the משנה so it holds together as one view.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא כּוּלָּהּ רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הִיא,
phrases.english: Rather, the entire mishna is Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,
and it is missing words, and this is what it teaches:
These are not paid.
In what case is this said?
When there are no witnesses to the divorce there,
but if there are witnesses to the divorce there —
she collects the additional sum.
And the main sum: if she produces a bill of divorce, she collects;

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי לָא מַפְּקָא גִּיטָּא — לָא גָּבְיָא.
phrases.english: and if she does not produce a bill of divorce, she does not collect.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא כּוּלָּהּ רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הִיא, וְחַסּוֹרֵי מִיחַסְּרָא וְהָכִי קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty by rebuilding the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: חסורי מיחסרא: filling in missing words so the whole משנה follows one תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first part and the last part of the משנה were thought to deal with different situations and different views.
steps.terutzMaskana: The whole משנה is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. Without witnesses she gets nothing; with witnesses she gets the תוספת, and the main sum only with a גט.

steps.title: From the time of danger she collects even without a גט
steps.stepSummary: The rebuilt משנה ends: from the time of danger onward, she collects even the main sum without a גט, as רבן שמעון בן גמליאל taught.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from the time of danger and on, even if she does not show a גט, she collects. For רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: From the time of danger and on, a woman collects her כתובה without a גט, and a lender collects without a פרוזבול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes rebuilding the משנה. It shows that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's ruling in the last clause fits as the final level.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In times of danger people could not safely keep documents. So the rule requiring a גט for the main sum is relaxed, and witnesses to the divorce are enough. The last clause now fits smoothly into the משנה, which answers the difficulty from step 2.

keyTerms.meaning: From the time of danger and onward

steps.whatToRemember: Under רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's reading there are three levels. With no witnesses, she collects nothing. With witnesses, she collects the תוספת, and the main sum only with a גט. From the time of danger onward, witnesses are enough even for the main sum.

phrases.english: And from the time of danger and onward,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא מַפְּקָא גִּיטָּא — גָּבְיָא.
phrases.english: even though she does not produce a bill of divorce, she collects.
phrases.notes: This means the main sum too, since there are witnesses to the divorce.

phrases.english: As Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
From the time of danger and onward
a woman collects her marriage contract without a bill of divorce,
and a creditor collects without a prosbol.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִן הַסַּכָּנָה וְאֵילָךְ, אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא מַפְּקָא גִּיטָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the rebuilt משנה begun in step 3.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: From the time of danger onward, a woman with witnesses to her divorce collects even the main sum of her כתובה without a גט, following רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

steps.title: Can a widow collect twice, once with death witnesses and once with a hidden divorce document?
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא and רב אסי ask רב how a widow collects, and point to a danger that she could collect twice.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא and רב אסי said to רב: You said that a גט collects the main sum. Then how does a widow from נשואין collect? With witnesses that her husband died. But let us worry that maybe he divorced her before he died. Then she could bring out the גט and collect with it a second time!
steps.whatsHappening: Two students challenge their teacher רב. If a גט is what collects the main sum, a widow might collect once as a widow and again with a secret גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רב's view the גט itself is proof for collecting the main sum. A widow has no גט, so she collects with עדי מיתה. But nothing stops her from also holding a גט from an earlier divorce, and producing it later to collect again from the heirs.

keyTerms.meaning: A divorce document lets her collect the main sum of the כתובה
A widow whose husband died after the full marriage
Witnesses who testify that the husband died

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרִי לֵיהּ רַב כָּהֲנָא וְרַב אַסִּי לְרַב:
phrases.english: Rav Kahana and Rav Asi said to Rav:
According to you, who said
that a bill of divorce collects the main sum,
phrases.notes: The main sum is the basic amount of the כתובה, as opposed to the extra amount the husband added on his own.

phrases.english: a widow from marriage, with what does she collect?
With witnesses to the death.
But let us worry that perhaps he divorced her,
and she will bring out the bill of divorce and collect with it?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge against רב's own statement from earlier on the daf: in a place where no כתובה is written, a גט alone collects the main sum. It tests that statement against the case of a widow.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's position that a גט collects the main sum of the כתובה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the גט is the tool for collecting, a widow who collected with עדי מיתה could later produce a hidden גט and collect again.

steps.title: She lived with her husband until he died
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that we only rely on death witnesses for a woman who was living with her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are talking about a woman who was living with her husband.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers that the worry does not apply. She was living with her husband right up to his death, so clearly he never divorced her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she lived in his home as his wife until he died, there is no realistic chance he had divorced her. So she cannot have a hidden גט to use later.

keyTerms.meaning: Living with her husband as his wife
In a case of a woman who is living (with him)

phrases.english: With a woman who lives under her husband.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the worry of step 5 by limiting the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any widow could be hiding a גט from an earlier divorce.
steps.terutzMaskana: A widow who lived with her husband until his death was obviously not divorced, so there is no hidden גט.

steps.title: Maybe he divorced her right before he died
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: maybe the divorce happened just before death, while she was still at home.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe he divorced her close to his death!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's answer. Even a woman living with her husband could have been divorced quietly at the very end of his life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Living together only proves there was no divorce long before. A last-minute divorce near death would leave no outside signs, so the risk of collecting twice comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: Close to the time of death

phrases.english: But perhaps he divorced her near his death!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that a woman living with her husband was surely not divorced.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A divorce given just before death would not show, so she could still hold a hidden גט.

steps.title: He brought the loss on himself
steps.stepSummary: If he divorced her secretly right before death, he caused his own loss.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is the one who caused a loss to himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that we do not need to protect against this case. A husband who divorced her quietly at the end caused his own loss.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The court does not have to guard against every unusual case. If the husband acted in a way that let her collect twice, the loss comes from his own actions.

phrases.english: He is the one who caused a loss to himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Placing the responsibility on the husband
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The court must protect the estate even from a secret divorce near death.
steps.terutzMaskana: No protection is needed there, because the husband caused his own loss.

steps.title: What about a widow from betrothal?
steps.stepSummary: A widow from אירוסין never lived with her husband, so the earlier answer does not protect against her collecting twice.
steps.simpleTranslation: A widow from אירוסין, with what does she collect? With witnesses to the death. But let us worry that maybe he divorced her, and she will bring out the גט and collect again!
steps.whatsHappening: The question comes back for a different kind of widow, one whose husband died during אירוסין. The answer of step 6 does not help here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ארוסה does not yet live with her husband. So we cannot say she was 'living with him', and nothing shows whether he divorced her. She could collect with עדי מיתה and then produce a hidden גט.

keyTerms.meaning: A widow whose husband died after betrothal but before the full marriage
Betrothal, the first stage of marriage, before living together

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think this is just a repeat of step 5. The point is that the answer of step 6, that she lived with him, cannot work for an ארוסה, who never lived with him.

phrases.english: A widow from betrothal, with what does she collect?
With witnesses to the death,
but let us worry that perhaps he divorced her,
and she will bring out the bill of divorce and collect!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the answer of step 6 does not cover every widow.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that we rely on her living with her husband.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An ארוסה never lived with her husband, so the double-collection risk returns.

steps.title: Where there is no other way, the court writes a receipt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new answer: whenever there is no other protection, the court writes a שובר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: where it is not possible otherwise, we write a receipt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the earlier approach and gives a new rule. When there is no other way to prevent double collection, she signs a receipt when she is paid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The heirs keep the שובר as proof that she was already paid. If she later brings out a גט, they show the receipt. This solves the ארוסה case directly.

keyTerms.meaning: A receipt showing that payment was made
Where it is not possible (to protect in another way)

phrases.english: Rather: in a place where it is not possible,
phrases.notes: He means: where there is no other way to know she was already paid.

phrases.english: we write a receipt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בִּמְקוֹם דְּלָא אֶפְשָׁר כָּתְבִינַן שׁוֹבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9 with a new, wider rule instead of limiting the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We needed an outside sign, like living together, to rule out a hidden גט.
steps.terutzMaskana: Wherever no such sign exists, a שובר protects the heirs from paying twice.

steps.title: Proof from the death witnesses themselves
steps.stepSummary: Without a receipt, even death witnesses could be used in one court after another, so receipts must be written.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you do not say so, then with the death witnesses themselves we should worry. Maybe she will bring the death witnesses to this court and collect, and then bring them again to another court and collect.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the receipt rule. Even without any גט, the same death witnesses could be brought to many courts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עדי מיתה could be used again and again in different courts. Since the law clearly lets a widow collect with עדי מיתה, there must already be a system of receipts that stops this. So receipts are a normal tool.

keyTerms.meaning: For if you do not say so

phrases.english: For if you do not say so,
with the death witnesses themselves, let us worry
that perhaps she will bring out death witnesses
in this court and collect,

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲדַר מַפְּקָא בְּבֵי דִינָא אַחֲרִינָא וְגָבְיָא.
phrases.english: and then bring them out again in another court and collect.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the receipt rule of step 10.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a שובר is written wherever there is no other protection.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Logic: עדי מיתה could be reused in many courts, so receipts must already be the system.

steps.title: Conclusion: receipts are written wherever needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא firmly concludes that wherever there is no other protection, a receipt is written.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, certainly: where it is not possible otherwise, we write a receipt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes this section by restating the rule, now proven. A שובר is written wherever there is no other protection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'certainly' shows the proof of step 11 settled the matter. So רב's view, that a גט collects the main sum, is safe. The widow, including an ארוסה, signs a receipt when she collects.
steps.whatToRemember: The challenge to רב is solved with a practical tool. Wherever there is no other way to block double collection, the widow signs a שובר, a receipt.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a general principle that a receipt is used to prevent double collection wherever nothing else protects the payer.

phrases.english: Rather, certainly, in a place where it is not possible,
we write a receipt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא וַדַּאי בִּמְקוֹם דְּלָא אֶפְשָׁר כָּתְבִינַן שׁוֹבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restates the rule of step 10 as settled after the proof of step 11.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Wherever there is no other way to prevent a woman from collecting her כתובה twice, the court writes a שובר. This protects רב's view that a גט collects the main sum.

steps.title: Where do we know a widow from betrothal gets a כתובה?
steps.stepSummary: מר קשישא asks רב אשי for the source that a woman widowed during אירוסין is entitled to a כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר קשישא, son of רב חסדא, said to רב אשי: How do we know that a widow from betrothal has a כתובה?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question opens. The earlier discussion took for granted that a widow from betrothal collects a כתובה, and now someone asks where that rule comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Maybe the רבנן only set up the כתובה for a fully married woman, so a betrothed woman would get nothing. The question asks for a source that covers the betrothal stage too.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman whose husband died after betrothal but before the full marriage
The marriage contract that guarantees the wife money if the marriage ends

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מָר קַשִּׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Mar the Elder, son of Rav Chisda, said to Rav Ashi:
A widow from betrothal,
from where do we know that she has a marriage contract?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָנָה מִן הָאֵירוּסִין, מְנָלַן דְּאִית לַהּ כְּתוּבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of an assumption used in step 9, that a widow from betrothal collects a כתובה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that the כתובה rule applies to a woman widowed during אירוסין.

steps.title: A suggested proof from a משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a proof from a משנה: a woman widowed or divorced, whether from betrothal or from marriage, collects everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the source is this משנה: 'If she was widowed or divorced, whether from betrothal or from marriage, she collects everything'...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible source, a משנה that mentions a widow from betrothal collecting. The proof will be checked in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה clearly puts betrothal and marriage side by side and says she collects. At first glance, that seems to answer the question directly.

keyTerms.meaning: If you would say (introduces a suggestion that will be checked)

phrases.english: If we say it is from this:
If she was widowed or divorced,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין מִן הָאֵירוּסִין בֵּין מִן הַנִּשּׂוּאִין,
phrases.english: whether from betrothal or from marriage,
she collects everything —
phrases.notes: "Everything" means the basic amount plus any extra the husband added on his own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to the question in step 13.
steps.raayaObject: That a widow from betrothal has a כתובה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: 'נתארמלה או נתגרשה, בין מן האירוסין בין מן הנשואין, גובה את הכל.'

steps.title: Maybe he wrote her a כתובה on his own
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed off: the משנה may be talking about a case where the husband chose to write her a כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps it is a case where he wrote her a כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof. The משנה might be about a man who decided on his own to write a כתובה during betrothal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he wrote one, of course she collects, because she holds a signed document. That does not show that the רבנן give her a כתובה automatically when none was written.
steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether a written כתובה works. It is whether a betrothed woman has a כתובה by rabbinic rule even when nothing was written.

phrases.english: Perhaps it is where he wrote one for her.
phrases.notes: He wrote her a כתובה by choice, not because the רבנן required it at betrothal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from step 14 by reading the משנה as a narrower case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the משנה is rejected, but not the rule itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה could be about a written כתובה, so it does not show a rabbinic right to one without a document.

steps.title: But then why would the משנה need to say it?
steps.stepSummary: An objection to the push-off: if he wrote her a כתובה, it is obvious that she collects, so why would the משנה teach it?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: if he wrote it for her, what is the point of saying it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a likely objection to step 15. If the husband wrote a document, the משנה would be teaching something obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה usually does not state something obvious. So reading it as a case of a written document seems to make the משנה pointless, which would bring back the original proof.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (introduces an expected objection)
What is there to say? It is obvious

phrases.english: And if you would say:
If he wrote it for her,
what is the point of stating it!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: אִי כְּתַב לַהּ, מַאי לְמֵימְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the push-off in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of the משנה as a case of a written כתובה (step 15).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a document was written, collecting is obvious, so the משנה would be teaching nothing.

steps.title: It comes to reject רבי אלעזר בן עזריה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches 'everything' to reject רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, who holds that the husband wrote the extra amount only on condition that he would marry her.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to exclude the view of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, who said he wrote it for her only on condition that he would marry her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objection in step 16. Even with a written כתובה, the משנה teaches something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה holds that the extra amount was promised only for a completed marriage, so a woman widowed during betrothal would not collect it. The משנה says she collects 'everything,' extra included, which disagrees with him. So the 'written כתובה' reading still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude, meaning to reject another opinion
A תנא who limits the extra amount to a completed marriage
Brings her in, meaning fully marries her

phrases.english: It comes to exclude the view of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya,
who said: He did not write it for her
except on condition that he would marry her.
phrases.notes: He is talking about the extra amount the husband added on top of the basic כתובה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection in step 16 and keeps the push-off from step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finds a new point in the משנה by showing which opinion it rejects.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A written כתובה makes the משנה's ruling obvious.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה teaches that even the extra amount is collected, against רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.

steps.title: The word 'everything' supports the written-כתובה reading
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's wording supports the idea that he wrote a כתובה, because 'collects everything' only makes sense if there is a written extra amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording is also precise, since it teaches 'she collects everything.' If he wrote her a כתובה, that explains 'everything.' But if he did not write one, what does 'everything' mean? She only has a מנה or two hundred!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now shows that the משנה's own words point toward the reading from step 15.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without a written document, a woman only gets the fixed rabbinic amount of 100 or 200 זוז, so there is no 'everything' to speak of. The word 'everything' suggests a written extra amount, so the משנה is no proof for the case where nothing was written.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording is also precise, meaning the text itself supports this
100 or 200 זוז, the fixed amount of a כתובה

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה about 'collecting everything' cannot prove that a betrothed widow has a כתובה, because it is probably talking about a husband who wrote one.

phrases.english: It is also precise, as it teaches:
She collects everything.
Granted, if you say that he wrote it for her —
that is why she collects everything.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ דְּלָא כְּתַב לַהּ.
phrases.english: But if you say that he did not write it for her,
what is the meaning of "she collects everything"?
She only has a maneh or two hundred!
phrases.notes: These are the set amounts of the רבנן, so there is nothing extra to call "everything."

steps.triggerLanguage: דַּיְקָא נָמֵי, דְּקָתָנֵי: גּוֹבָה אֶת הַכֹּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds support from the wording for the push-off in step 15, which ends the first proof.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה is talking about a case where he wrote her a כתובה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The phrase 'גובה את הכל' in the משנה.

steps.title: A new proof from רב חייא בר אבין's ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: A new source: רב חייא בר אבין taught that if a betrothed husband dies, she collects her כתובה, even though they do not mourn or inherit each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the source is what רב חייא בר אבין taught: For his betrothed wife, he is not an אונן and does not become impure for her. Likewise, she is not an אוננת and does not become impure for him. If she dies, he does not inherit her. If he dies, she collects her כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the first proof failed, the גמרא brings a different source that seems to answer the question in step 13 directly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא is about betrothal only and lists ways a betrothed couple is not yet treated as married. Even so, it says she collects her כתובה when he dies. Because it says nothing about a written document, it seems to show she has a כתובה by rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A betrothed woman, before the full marriage
A mourner on the day of a close relative's death, before burial
Becomes impure, said of a כהן who may become impure for close relatives

steps.whyThisMatters: The ברייתא treats a betrothed couple as not yet married for mourning and inheritance, yet says she collects a כתובה. The next step questions whether this really proves an automatic right.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶלָּא, מִדְּתָנֵי רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין:
phrases.english: But rather, it is from what Rav Chiyya bar Avin taught:
His betrothed wife:
he is not an acute mourner for her, and does not become impure for her.
And likewise she:
she is not an acute mourner and does not become impure for him.
If she dies, he does not inherit from her;
if he dies, she collects her marriage contract.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא, מִדְּתָנֵי רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected proof (steps 14-18) with a new source for the question in step 13.
steps.raayaObject: That a widow from betrothal has a כתובה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רב חייא בר אבין: 'מת הוא — גובה כתובתה.'

steps.title: Maybe he wrote her a כתובה here too
steps.stepSummary: The proof from רב חייא בר אבין is pushed off. Maybe that case is one where the husband chose to write her a כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps it is a case where he wrote her a כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the new proof from step 19 using the same push-off it used before. Maybe the husband wrote her a כתובה on his own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof wanted to show that every widow from אירוסין gets a כתובה automatically. If the husband personally wrote one, she collects because of what he wrote, not because of a general rule. So the source proves nothing about the general rule.

keyTerms.meaning: That he wrote for her (a כתובה)

phrases.english: Perhaps it is where he wrote [a כתובה] for her.
phrases.notes: This is the same push-off the גמרא used back in step 15, now applied to the new source.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 19.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from רב חייא בר אבין's teaching.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The teaching may be about a case where the husband personally wrote a כתובה, so it does not show an automatic right.

steps.title: If he wrote it, why teach it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises the expected objection: if he wrote her a כתובה, it is obvious that she collects, so what is the teaching adding?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say: if he wrote it for her, what is the point of saying it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא imagines someone objecting to the push-off. If the husband wrote a כתובה, of course she collects, so why would anyone bother teaching it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same kind of objection as step 16. A teaching should tell us something new. If it only says that a written document gets paid, it seems pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (introduces an expected objection)
What is there to say? It is obvious

phrases.english: And if you would say: if he wrote it for her,
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: אִי כְּתַב לַהּ מַאי לְמֵימְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the push-off of step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רב חייא בר אבין's teaching is about a husband who wrote a כתובה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If he wrote one, her collecting is obvious, so the teaching would be pointless.

steps.title: The point is that he does not inherit her
steps.stepSummary: The teaching is still needed: even though he wrote her a כתובה, if she dies he does not inherit her.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed to teach that if she dies, he does not inherit her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objection. The new point of the teaching is not that she collects, but that if she dies, he does not inherit her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Writing a כתובה might seem to make her fully like a married wife, so one might think he would inherit her. The teaching says he does not, since they are only betrothed. With this, the push-off stands, and the גמרא is left with no source proving that a widow from אירוסין automatically gets a כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary for him (to teach)

steps.whatToRemember: Every proof was pushed off with 'maybe he wrote her a כתובה.' The question of whether a widow from אירוסין automatically gets a כתובה is left without a source.

phrases.english: If she dies, he does not inherit her:
that is what he needed [to teach].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 21 and closes the search for a source.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finds a different novel point in the teaching.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since he wrote her a כתובה, she would be treated like a full wife, and he would inherit her.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even with a written כתובה, a betrothed husband does not inherit her, and that is the teaching's purpose.

steps.title: Could she collect twice with one גט?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן asks רב הונא: according to רב, a woman collects the basic כתובה with just a גט. So she might collect in one court and then again in another. Tearing the גט won't work, because she needs it to remarry.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to רב הונא: according to רב, who said that with a גט she collects the main sum, we should worry that she will bring the גט to this court and collect, and then bring it to another court and collect again. And if you say we tear it, she will say: I need it to marry with.
steps.whatsHappening: A new discussion opens. רב נחמן points out a problem with רב's view that a גט alone lets her collect: one גט could be used to collect in many courts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, when a debt document is paid, the court tears it so it can't be used again. Here the גט is also her proof that she is divorced, so she needs it whole in order to remarry. That seems to leave no way to stop a second collection.

keyTerms.meaning: With a גט she collects the main (basic) sum of the כתובה

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן לְרַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said to Rav Huna:
According to Rav, who said that with a bill of divorce she collects the main sum,
let us worry that perhaps she will bring out the bill of divorce
in this court and collect,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָדְרָא מַפְּקָא בְּבֵי דִינָא אַחֲרִינָא וְגָבְיָא?
phrases.english: and then again bring it out in another court and collect?
And if you say that we tear it,
phrases.notes: Courts usually tear a paid-up document so it can't be used again.

phrases.english: she will say: I need it in order to get married with it.
phrases.notes: She means she needs the גט to show she is divorced and free to remarry.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן לְרַב הוּנָא: לְרַב דְּאָמַר גֵּט גּוֹבָה עִיקָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the previous search for a source ended.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that a גט alone lets her collect the basic כתובה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One גט could be used in several courts, and the usual fix of tearing the document fails because she needs the גט to remarry.

steps.title: Tear it and write the reason on the back
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers: the court tears the גט and writes on its back that it was torn only to stop a second collection, not because it is invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: We tear it and write on its back: 'We tore this גט not because it is an invalid גט, but so that she will not come back and collect with it another time.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא solves the problem. The court tears the גט and adds a note on the back that explains why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The tear stops her from collecting again, because no court will pay on a torn document. The written note keeps the גט useful as proof of divorce, since anyone reading it knows the tear does not mean the גט was bad. Both needs are met at once.
steps.whatToRemember: A paid גט is torn so it can't be used to collect again, and a note on the back keeps it valid as proof that she is divorced.

phrases.english: That we tear it
and write on its back:
'This bill of divorce, we tore it
not because it is an invalid bill of divorce,
but so that she will not come back
and collect with it another time.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב נחמן's challenge in step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical solution that meets both concerns.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Tearing the גט would ruin her proof of divorce, so it can't be done.
steps.terutzMaskana: Tear it and write the reason on the back. It can't be used to collect again, but it still proves the divorce.

steps.title: New משנה: two גיטין and two כתובות
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: a woman who holds two גיטין and two כתובות collects two כתובות.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Two bills of divorce and two כתובות: she collects two כתובות.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. A woman was divorced, remarried the same man, and was divorced again, and she shows two גיטין and two כתובות. She collects both כתובות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Holding both sets of documents shows that the first כתובה was never paid. If it had been paid, the first כתובה document would have been torn or returned. So she gets paid for both marriages.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Two bills of divorce and two marriage contracts:
phrases.notes: She married and divorced the same man twice, so she has a set of documents from each marriage.

phrases.english: she collects two marriage contracts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman holding two גיטין and two כתובות from the same man collects both כתובות.

steps.title: When she collects only one כתובה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists three cases where the woman collects only one כתובה, because a man who remarries his wife relies on the first כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she has two marriage contracts and one bill of divorce, or one marriage contract and two bills of divorce, or a marriage contract, a bill of divorce, and proof of death, she collects only one marriage contract. This is because a man who divorces his wife and then takes her back remarries her based on the first marriage contract.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues from the case of two גיטין and two כתובות. It now gives three cases where she collects only one כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To collect two כתובות, she needs proof of two marriages and two endings. With two כתובות but only one גט, the marriage ended only once. With two גיטין but only one כתובה, there is no second כתובה, because the remarriage ran on the first one.

keyTerms.meaning: on the basis of / with the understanding of
death (here, proof that the husband died)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that two גיטין automatically mean two payments. When he remarried her without writing a new כתובה, the first כתובה simply carried over, so there is still only one כתובה to collect.

phrases.english: Two marriage contracts and one bill of divorce,
or one marriage contract and two bills of divorce,
or a marriage contract, a bill of divorce, and death —
phrases.notes: "Death" means proof that the husband died after he remarried her.

phrases.english: she collects only one marriage contract.
For one who divorces his wife and takes her back —
takes her back on the basis of the first marriage contract.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה begun in step 25 by giving the contrasting cases where she collects only once.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Without two full marriage-and-ending pairs, she collects only one כתובה, because a remarriage relies on the first כתובה.

steps.title: May she choose which כתובה to collect with?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether, with two כתובות and one גט, she may collect with whichever כתובה she prefers.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: If she wants to collect with this one, she collects. If she wants to collect with that one, she collects?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the משנה. It asks whether she has the choice of which of her two כתובות to use. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said she collects only one כתובה but did not say which one. If she may choose, she could pick the larger amount or the earlier date. The assumption that she may choose leads straight into a problem with רב נחמן's rule.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
If she wants, she collects with this one,
phrases.notes: "This one" and "that one" are her two כתובות, for example one with a larger amount and one with an earlier date.

phrases.english: and if she wants, she collects with that one?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reads the משנה's case of two כתובות and one גט as giving her a free choice of which one to use.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the woman may choose which of her two כתובות to collect with.

steps.title: Does this contradict רב נחמן's rule that a second document cancels the first?
steps.stepSummary: If she may use either כתובה, this seems to refute רב נחמן in the name of שמואל, who says a second document cancels the first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this is a refutation of what רב נחמן said in the name of שמואל. For רב נחמן said in the name of שמואל: when two documents are issued one after the other, the second cancels the first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem. If the first כתובה is still usable, that seems to go against רב נחמן's rule that a later document cancels an earlier one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב נחמן, the second כתובה should cancel the first, so she should have only the second one. The משנה seems to let the first one stay valid, and that clashes with his rule.

phrases.english: Let us say this is a refutation
of what Rav Nachman said in the name of Shmuel.
For Rav Nachman said in the name of Shmuel:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵי שְׁטָרוֹת הַיּוֹצְאִין בָּזֶה אַחַר זֶה,
phrases.english: Two documents that are issued one after the other,
phrases.notes: He means two documents recording the same deal, written on different dates.

phrases.english: the second cancels the first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the choice assumed in step 27 against an established rule about documents.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's rule in the name of שמואל that a second document cancels the first.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the first כתובה can still be used after a second was written, then a second document does not cancel the first, which goes against רב נחמן.

steps.title: A second document that adds something does not cancel the first
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא said that רב נחמן agrees a second document that adds something is an addition, not a cancellation. Our case is one where the second כתובה added to her amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: Was it not stated about this: רב פפא said, רב נחמן agrees that if he added a palm tree in the second document, he wrote it as an addition. Here too, it is a case where he added for her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב נחמן. It points out that his rule has a known limit, and our case falls within that limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A second document cancels the first only when it simply repeats the same deal. If it adds something, like an extra palm tree, it is clearly meant as an addition, so both documents stand. Here, the second כתובה added money for her, so the first כתובה is not cancelled and the משנה does not contradict רב נחמן.
steps.whatToRemember: A second document cancels the first only if it adds nothing. If it adds something, it was written as an addition and the first stays valid. That is why she may use either כתובה.

phrases.english: Was it not stated about this:
Rav Pappa said:
And Rav Nachman agrees
that if he added a palm tree in it,
phrases.notes: "In it" means in the second document, which included a tree the first one did not.

phrases.english: he wrote it as an addition.
Here too, it is a case where he added for her.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו אִתְּמַר עֲלַהּ אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 28 by limiting רב נחמן's rule and placing the משנה's case inside that limit.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the rule and redefining the case: the second document added something, so it does not cancel the first.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every second document cancels the first, so the first כתובה should be void.
steps.terutzMaskana: A second document that adds something is an addition. Since the second כתובה added money, both stand and she may choose either one.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches a general rule about documents: a later document is read as cancelling an earlier one only when it adds nothing new.

steps.title: A ברייתא introduces a woman with a divorce document, a marriage contract, and proof of death
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא. It describes a woman who brings a גט, a כתובה, and evidence that her husband died. The ruling has not been given yet.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: if a woman brought a גט, a כתובה, and proof of her husband's death...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts quoting a new ברייתא and describes the case. This line is only setup, and the ruling follows in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The woman holds papers that point two ways. The גט shows she was divorced, while the proof of death suggests she was still married when he died. The ברייתא will tell us how to handle her כתובה claim in this situation.

keyTerms.meaning: "The רבנן taught." This opens a ברייתא, a teaching from the time of the משנה that is not in the משנה itself.
She brought out, meaning she showed the documents in בית דין.
Death. Here it means proof, such as witnesses, that the husband died.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
If she produced a bill of divorce and a marriage contract
and death,
phrases.notes: Literally "and death." It means she also brought proof, like witnesses, that her husband died.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הוֹצִיאָה גֵּט וּכְתוּבָּה וּמִיתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After resolving the two-כתובות question with רב פפא's answer, the גמרא brings a related ברייתא about a woman holding several documents.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet. The ברייתא sets up a case of a woman who brings a גט, a כתובה, and proof of her husband's death. The ruling follows.
